title: Level 3 Crispy Tomato-Breaded Garlic Parm Chicken Wings
summary: Dry-cured wings breaded in flour, a tomato-paste egg wash and panko, double-fried, then tossed in a creamy blender garlic-Parmigiano emulsion with fresh herbs, shallot and Fresno chile.
notes: Video: 'The Best Chicken Wings At Home (3 Levels)' on the Joshua Weissman Recipes channel (UCUAg71CJEvFdOnujmep1Svw). Written recipe for the same video (it links this video): https://www.joshuaweissman.com/recipes/the-best-chicken-wings-at-home-3-levels-recipe (one page for all three levels: serves 4, prep 20 min, cook 45 min). Level 3 of 3. Servings: he says 2 lb of wings is enough for about two people ('a pound per person'), and every level uses 2 lb, so we use 2 servings (stated, video); the written recipe says 4. Times are left null: the page's 20 + 45 minutes cover all three levels together and are not split by level; the cure also needs 1-2 hours, ideally overnight. The cure (salt and baking soda) stays on the wings and is counted in full. The 2 lb is the as-bought weight of whole wings with bone (and tips, which he says you may remove), entered as bought (house rule 12); the lead converts it to edible weight. Absorbed oil uses the as-bought weight. The wings are deep-fried in vegetable oil: the pot of oil is excluded and absorbed oil is added at 10% of the raw weight with any counted coating (house rule; arithmetic on that line). The video states the sauce and breading amounts; the written recipe matches it (it marks the corn syrup optional and calls the shallot small and the eggs large). Our estimates: 25 g for the shallot (USDA has no per-shallot weight), 1 Tbsp for the splash of water, 1/2 tsp kosher salt and 1/4 tsp pepper to season the full sauce batch (house salt rule; 50% of each counted with the sauce). Sauce: he states no share used, so 50% of the tossed garlic parm sauce is counted (house rule 10); text keeps the full batch. Breading: flour and panko counted at 25%, the egg wash (eggs, water, onion powder, tomato paste, salt) at 50% (house rule). Absorbed oil: 115 g, applied once although the wings are fried twice. Not counted: the pecorino or Parmigiano and chives used to finish (no amounts), and dried thyme, a named alternative. Proxies: Dijon uses USDA prepared yellow mustard; panko uses USDA plain dry breadcrumbs, which weigh more per cup than panko.

steps.text: If using whole wings, cut away the flap of skin at the joint, bend the joint until it pops, and cut through it to separate the drum. Do the same at the next joint to take off the tip if you like (freeze tips for stock).
Toss the drums and flats with the kosher salt and baking soda, rubbing it in well. Arrange on a wire rack over a baking sheet and refrigerate uncovered 1-2 hours, ideally overnight, to dry the skin.
Sauce: in a blender (or a bowl with a whisk), combine the egg yolks, Dijon, corn syrup, lemon juice, garlic, thyme and Parmigiano. Blend on medium to medium-high until as smooth as possible.
With the blender running, stream in the oil slowly until it is all added and the sauce is thick and creamy, like mayonnaise. Pour into a bowl.
Add the shallot, Fresno chile, rosemary and parsley, season with salt and pepper, and mix. Taste and adjust the seasoning now, before it goes on the wings.
Breading: set out the flour; whisk the eggs with a splash of water, the onion powder, tomato paste and about 1 tsp salt until smooth; and set out the panko.
Working a few wings at a time, toss them in the flour and shake off the excess, then coat in the tomato egg wash, then tumble in the panko and press it on so they are fully covered.
Fry in 2-3 batches of similar-sized pieces at 325°F, about 5 minutes, until they reach at least 165°F inside. Remove, and repeat.
Raise the oil to 350°F and fry the wings again 1-3 minutes, until deep golden brown and crisp, without burning them.

In a large bowl, pour the garlic parm sauce around the edge and a little on top, then fold the wings gently (or brush the sauce on) so the breading stays intact. Plate, and finish with grated pecorino or Parmigiano and sliced chives.
